target.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to SharePoint file send requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending files to MS Teams group chats or channels could see delivery hang indefinitely when a SharePoint or Graph request stalled before headers or while reading the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

SharePoint file-send calls now reuse the existing MS Teams request timeout budget around the full fetch lifecycle, including response body reads. The aborting timeout helper now lives in the existing MS Teams request-timeout owner instead of as a local graph-upload-only helper.

## User Impact

File sends through MS Teams group and channel paths fail fast instead of leaving the delivery pending forever when Microsoft Graph or SharePoint stops responding.

## Evidence

Exact head after CI/proof refresh and normal upstream/main merge: `0ae42ef74ce58ae97ee39070c8dd855b2d71b73c`.

Implementation updates after ClawSweeper/CI review:

- Fixed CI lint failure `typescript(prefer-promise-reject-errors)` in `extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts`; the hanging-fetch test now rejects with an `Error` even if an AbortSignal reason is not an Error.
- Moved the aborting SharePoint timeout wrapper into `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts`, the existing MS Teams timeout owner, and kept `graph-upload.ts` as the SharePoint request caller.
- Updated the branch with a normal merge from `upstream/main`; no rebase or force-push.

Validation run:

```text
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD -- extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts
-> clean

node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts
-> clean

node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts
-> All matched files use the correct format.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts
-> 1 file passed, 9 tests passed
```

Controlled partial SharePoint/Graph stalled-transport proof:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module
```

Harness shape: production `uploadAndShareSharePoint()` and `getDriveItemProperties()` helpers, real Node HTTP loopback server, real `fetch()` transport to loopback, redacted token provider, and a transport shim that redirects Microsoft Graph/SharePoint URLs to loopback paths. This is intentionally not described as a live Microsoft tenant run.

Observed behavior:

- A SharePoint upload that stalls before response headers rejects after the existing 30s MS Teams request budget.
- A group-chat upload flow that succeeds through upload and member lookup but stalls while reading the `createLink` response body also rejects after the same budget.
- The native file-card metadata request (`getDriveItemProperties`) rejects after the same budget when it stalls before response headers.
- The loopback server observes client-side connection closure after each timed-out request.

Known limits:

- This is stronger than the previous mocked unit-only proof because it runs production MS Teams graph-upload helpers through real HTTP loopback stalls, but it is still not a live Microsoft Graph/SharePoint tenant proof.
- No Microsoft tenant credentials were available in this environment, so a real group/channel file send against Microsoft services remains untested.
- Remote Crabbox/Testbox proof was unavailable because the selected `crabbox` binary failed basic `--version`/`--help` sanity checks; this used the documented narrow local fallback plus GitHub CI.
